digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate impact model and calibration
propositions: The divergent_implementation axis misfires on 90% of omitted-scope findings because its ordinal grade scheme (none/low/medium/high) does not distinguish load-bearing divergences from cosmetic ones; it must be regrade to a closed Literal set separating contradicts_reality and omits_required_site (both 0.85 hard floor) from incomplete_enumeration (contribution below 0.60, never floors)

The impact_plan function currently resolves all axes through _SEV01 keyed only on ordinal grades; a schema-only change to symbolic grades would silently score all three as 0.0, causing the axis to stop firing entirely rather than flooring; the implementation must exclude divergent_implementation from _SEV01 and route it through a new DIVERGENCE_GRADE01 map mirroring the oracle-kind pattern

Rejecting Fix 2 (prod_impact hard floor at 0.70): a severity-band floor collides with the novelty_priority_floor convergence mechanism because production impact is orthogonal to novelty/carryover status, allowing findings to recur across remediation rounds with no author action that resolves them; Fix 1's semantic grading is bounded and inherently remediable

ADR 0054 must record an explicit rejection of purpose-built LLM eval suites and bulk re-review runs as calibration instruments, narrowing ADR 0036's A/B clause to only corpus replay and dogfood observation, with zero marginal LLM cost

All existing fixtures and consumers of divergent_implementation must migrate from ordinal grades to the closed Literal set; the Literal type makes low/medium/high parse errors so missed sites break CI, and prompt-side consumers (verifiers, G7) must state explicit kind mappings

Pre-landing corpus replay bounds the outcome within 81 newly-blocked findings at worst case (all grades→floor grades), far below the 113-finding over-fire of ungraded widening; real results determined by dogfooding per ADR 0054 §3(b).
